reference_items.stem:
A club has 86 members, and there are 14 more girls than boys. How many boys and how many girls are members of the club?

Show your work.

descriptors: 36 boys and 50 girls [Numerical method: e.g., 86 ÷ 2 = 43; 43 − 7 = 36 boys; 43 + 7 = 50 girls]
36 boys and 50 girls [Algebraic method: e.g., b + (b + 14) = 86; 2b = 72; b = 36; g = 36 + 14 = 50]
Other fully satisfactory method including “guess and check” with justification that 36 + 50 = 86
Either 36 boys or 50 girls, with or without another (incorrect) number
36 and 50 are given [Makes correct computations but reverses labels or does not include any mention of which is boys or girls]
36 boys and 50 girls, no method shown
Gives an algebraic equation or system of equations that can lead to the correct solution
Other partially correct

One of the numbers is 72 [Computes 86 − 14]

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

step1.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". In the GPCM, b - d1 is the ability at which earning the first point becomes more likely than earning no point, so a higher d1 means that this point is earned at a lower ability; the steps sum to 0. Choose the value closest to it.
